milestones.title: Plans 45.2-13, 45.2-16 and 45.2-07 hold every such file in quarantine for an exchange officer; the condition is reviewed with each partner's pinned anchors at the acceptance trial (45.2-12)

remediation: Partners whose systems are not like ours can send files whose label cannot be checked: a binding with no signature, a signature by an anchor your organization has not pinned for that partner, a form this version cannot check yet, a marking read from the file's text, or no label at all. Such files are held in quarantine in a protected cell at a provisional label, and an exchange officer confirms, raises or sets the label; a label lower than the sender's is refused. A person's confirmation is recorded as that person's act, never as a check of the file, so a mistaken confirmation is the risk that remains. Setting the label of an unlabelled arrival below its holding ceiling (the agreement's ceiling, released to no one) is not lowering: the holding label is your organization's protective default, not the sender's claim. Your organization's security officer accepts this condition; pinning each partner's signing anchors in exchangePartners turns claimed labels into checked ones. Source: .planning/phases/45.2-nato-and-five-eyes-exchange-part-2-ztdf-and-the-nato-texts/45.2-CONTEXT.md D-25, D-28 and D-29.
title: Labels on partner files that cannot be checked are confirmed by an exchange officer
